result.summary:
Independently read test/specs/REQ-043.md and all three test files (json_array_test.exs, engine/schemas_test.exs, engine/migrations_test.exs) directly, plus lib/letflow/design/req043-instance-engine-schema.md and the actual lib/letflow/engine/token.ex and task.ex sources (not TEST-DESIGNER's summary alone). All 5 checks pass: (a) every acceptance criterion (AC2 uq_instance_correlation, AC4 status enum, AC5 JSONArray round-trip, AC6 migrations/schema-per-tenant) has >=1 runnable, non-skipped test with a real failure mode -- confirmed by reading the assertions themselves, not just the spec's claims table; (b) grepped all three test files and the spec for '@tag :skip' / 'TODO' -- zero matches; (c) fixtures use Ecto.UUID.generate()/System.unique_integer per test, provisioned_tenant/0 provisions a fresh tenant+schema per call (not shared across a describe block) -- no hardcoded shared IDs; (d) every DB-touching test calls provisioned_tenant() itself and cleans up via on_exit/1, no test reads state another test wrote; (e) grepped for password/secret/postgres:// literals -- zero matches, DB access goes through Letflow.Repo/config/test.exs only. Also ran mix compile --warnings-as-errors myself (exit 0) as a cheap independent corroboration that the artefacts are real and consistent, not fabricated.

Verdict on the flagged MINOR item (AC3's 'rejects a disagreeing caller-supplied tenant_id' half): legitimate, honestly-handled scope boundary, not an excuse. Verified independently by reading lib/letflow/engine/token.ex and task.ex directly and via `ls lib/letflow/engine/` -- the directory contains only token.ex and task.ex, no engine.ex context module, confirming the design doc's own §6 point 2 claim that no public attrs-accepting function exists yet for a rejection test to exercise. Writing a test asserting Token.insert_changeset/2 rejects a disagreeing tenant_id would assert something false about the shipped code (the changeset has no FK/check-constraint/comparison logic on tenant_id at all) -- a real 'No Speculation' violation if written literally. The three substitute tests in migrations_test.exs's 'tenant_id internal-derivation contract' describe block are a sound handling of the gap: (1) positive derivation case proves the 'derived internally' half literally: (2) storage-isolation case proves schema-per-tenant does real isolation work independent of the tenant_id column; (3) the tripwire test explicitly asserts today's real accept-not-reject behavior with a comment stating it must fail the moment enforcement is added without updating it -- this is a deliberate regression guard, not a shrug. The gap is filed as a MINOR issue on the Step 3 handoff with a concrete recommendation (REQ-045's TEST-DESIGNER adds the literal test once a context-module function exists), matching core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence rule ('never resolve a conflict silently... record it in result.issues'). This is the correct behavior for a schema-only requirement, not a coverage gap.
